subject: management-of-business
title: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - buffer stock should never be touched, so ordering must wait until stock runs out

Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands.
Reorder when stock reaches the buffer stock, because the buffer is the order trigger
Order a fixed quantity every week and ignore the stock level

questions.misconception: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away. Reteach point: Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why stock must not be allowed to fall below the buffer stock of 250 units.
questions.answer: The buffer stock is the safety floor held against unexpected demand or late delivery, so falling below it risks a stock-out with nothing left to sell or use.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the buffer as a safety floor against delays and unexpected demand, not as spare stock.

questions.prompt: Usage is 125 units a day and the lead time is 2 days. How much stock is used during the lead time?
questions.feedback: Scene 3 shows the calculation: lead-time usage is 2 days x 125 units a day = 250 units, which is why the reorder level sits 250 units above the buffer.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state when the next order is placed after the delivery on day 6, and why.
questions.answer: The next order is placed on day 10, when falling stock again reaches the reorder level of 500 units, so the following delivery can land as stock bottoms out at the buffer.
questions.feedback: A strong answer gives the full chain in order - fall from day 6, reorder level reached on day 10, delivery after the 2-day lead time.
